[By Sri B.S. Sudhindra, Advocate] /Vs/ Defendants 1) Ms. Reeni, Age: Major, Incharge Head Mistress 2 OS.No. 2431/2024 Government High School Basaweshwaranagara, Bengaluru - 560079. 2) Smt. [D-1 to 6 by D.G.P.] Date of Institution of the suit : 01-04-2024 Nature of the Suit : Permanent injunction Date of commencement of recording of evidence : 12-08-2024 Date on which the Judgment was pronounced : 04-11-2024 3 OS.No. 2431/2024 Year/s Month/s Day/s Total Duration : 00 07 03 (S. texts.facts: This suit of the plaintiff is for permanent injunction restraining the defendants No.1 to 6 from interfering/disturbing with his peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property bearing school premises No.230, 3rd Stage, 3rd Division, 6th Main Road, situated inside the compound of the Government High School, Saneguruvanahalli, Basaweshwaranagara, Bengaluru, measuring East to West 10 feet and North to South 15 feet, consisting of one hall, kitchen, bath room built with bricks and cement, A.C. sheet roofing, door and windows of iron. The plaintiff's case in brief are as follows : 2(a). The plaintiff has filed this suit for permanent injunction. The father of plaintiff late Sri.Muniyappa rendered the service in Saneguruvanahalli Government High School as a Watchmen on honorary basis. His father was died on 23/12/2009. Thereafter, the plaintiff continued the service of his father as Watchman and taking care and safety of the school and also doing the work instructed by the school staffs, educational officers, teachers etc.,. 2(b). From the period of his father, the school authorities and educational department have provided an accommodation to his father in a portion of school premise i.e., suit schedule shed. Subsequently, the plaintiff and his family members continued, the school authorities as well as educational officers recognized his continuation in the schedule premise. The wife of the plaintiff OS.No. 2431/2024 Smt.Jayalakshmamma is working as Aaya in the High School and she had obtained Gas connection and Bank account in respect of schedule premises. 2(c). The defendant No.1 and 2 by influence and pressure from the politically motivated persons attempted to disturb and interfere with the plaintiff's possession over the schedule premises. The 1 st defendant in the month of December 2023, along with defendant No.2 created nuisance and threatened the plaintiff and his family members to dispossess them from the schedule premises and other defendants have not solved their problems. If the plaintiff and his family members are thrown out from the schedule premises, they will be on the street without food and shelter. 2(d). The defendants have issued notice to the plaintiff and made an attempt to disturb the physical possession and tried to remove the shed stayed in the OS.No. 2431/2024 schedule property. The complaint was lodged to jurisdictional police, but they refused to receive the same. Hence, filed this suit. 3. The defendants have filed written statement by contending that the plaintiff's suit is not maintainable. The plaintiff's wife Smt.Jayalakshmamma has been appointed as Aaya on temporary/contract basis on 17/08/1995 as Group-D employee at Government Model Primary School, Saneguruvanahalli. The plaintiff is presently residing in the school premises unauthorized manner causing trouble to academic activities of the school. The plaintiff and his wife claiming that they own the above said room of the school premises. The plaintiff has not been appointed as Watchman either from the School or Educational Department. Apart from Smt.Jayalakshmamma, Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/ 3 no other family members are rendering their service to the school. OS.No. 2431/2024 3(a). The plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands. The Government Mode Primary School and Government High School of Saneguruvanahalli for the benefit of children and school got sanctioned 8 rooms under 'Viveka Shala Yojane'. The defendant school has issued notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed and he requested 3 months time to vacate the same. The process of construction of the building has started and at that time, the present suit is filed and children academic progress is damaging. The children have no place to sit or for class process. In the SDMC and parents meeting dated 18/12/2023, decided to serve the notice to the plaintiff to vacate the shed. The plaintiff has no right, title and interest over the schedule premises. The defendant No.1 and 2 have no personal interest and no enmity against the plaintiff, they have been made parties in their individual capacity and prayed for dismissal of the suit. OS.No. 2431/2024 4. The plaintiff in his oral evidence deposed as per the plaint averments that he is residing in the suit schedule premises with his wife. His father Muniyappa was rendering service of Watchman of the school premises. After death of his father, he OS.No. 2431/2024 continued as Watchman on honorary basis without any salary. From 1983 father of plaintiff was rendering service. The defendants all of a sudden issued a notice for vacating the premises and interfering with his peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, has has no accommodation to reside. As such, he filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendants. 9. The DW.1 - 2nd defendant Head Master of Government High School, Saneguruvanahalli, Basaveshwaranagar, Bangalore, deposed the evidence as per the written statement contention that the plaintiff's wife was appointed as temporary/contract basis as Aya on 01-06-1995 and working as 'D' Group employee at Government Model Primary school, Saneguruvanahalli, receiving salary from Education department. Jayalakshmamma and her husband - plaintiff presently occupied the school premises in unauthorized manner and causing OS.No. 2431/2024 trouble to academic activities of the school. The plaintiff and his father have not been appointed as Watchman either from Education department or from the School or from the Villagers. The defendants or the Education department at no point of time appointed the plaintiff or his father for rendering service in the school. 9(a). The plaintiff who was running petty shop in the school premises in unauthorized manner. After noticing the same by the higher authorities, petty shop was closed as it was affecting the health and academic activities of the children. The premises in which the plaintiff and his wife have unauthorizedly occupied do not have separate way to ingress and egress from the shed, which is official school gate for children convenience. Under "Viveka Shala Yojane" eight rooms were sanctioned. As per the sanction of eight rooms for the purpose of construction, the premises in which the plaintiff and his wife is in OS.No. 2431/2024 occupation is required to be vacated and issued notice to the plaintiff's wife to vacate the shed, the plaintiff has sought 3 months time to vacate the premises. The meeting of SDMC and parent association was also convened, in which the plaintiff, his wife and son were also participated and did not vacate the premises. For construction of new 8 rooms, three old dilapidated rooms have been demolished. The school has no place for children to sit after class room closes. Around Rs.1 crore has been Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/ 5 sanctioned for construction of 8 rooms , if the construction is not carried out within stipulated time, the sanctioned amount would be elapsed. The children would be deprived of class rooms and affecting their academic activities.
texts.arguments: 10. The counsel for the plaintiff in support of his submissions argued that the plaintiff and his wife are in occupation of suit schedule property. The plaintiff's father since from 1983 was running service OS.No. 2431/2024 in the school as per the advise of the Villagers, as there was illegal activities were going on in the school premises. The plaintiff's father was asked to look after the school premises. Since then the father of plaintiff was stayed in the suit schedule premises and rendering service to the school as honorary as Watchman. The counsel further submits that after the death of father of plaintiff, the plaintiff continued to stay in the suit schedule premises with his wife, who is also working as Aya in the very same school appointed by the Education department. 10(a). The counsel submits that the defendants all of a sudden issued notice demanding the plaintiff to vacate the suit schedule premises and making illegal demand. The plaintiff has no other accommodation to stay. The suit schedule premises/shed has separate ingress and egress. The demolition of shed is not required for construction of 8 new class rooms to the children. The photographs are created by the OS.No. 2431/2024 defendants for the purpose of the case to show that the school has no class rooms and children are sitting outside the school. 10(b). The counsel further submitted that the plaintiff in order to show the possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property since long time, the bank pass book, gas bill address are shown as a suit schedule property. The photograph of Exs.P-8 and P-9 series would show the plaintiff and his wife are staying in the suit schedule premises without any hindrance and they have right to continue in the suit schedule premises. The defendants unnecessarily interfering and prayed to decree the suit. 11. The learned D.G.P. on behalf of the defendants submitted that the plaintiff is not at all connected to defendant school. His wife is working in the school appointed by the Education department as Aya. OS.No. 2431/2024 There is no post called Watchman in the school. The School or Education department have not appointed either father of the plaintiff or plaintiff as a Watchman to render service in the school. It is further submitted that the plaintiff has not placed any material to show that his father was rendering service in the school as Watchman and thereafter plaintiff. The wife of plaintiff was appointed as Aya in the year 1995 and she was transferred to this school subsequently. 11(a). It is further submitted that the Government had sanctioned 8 rooms under "Viveka Shala Yojane" an amount of Rs.1 crore was sanctioned. The dilapidated 3 class rooms have been demolished for the purpose of construction of 8 rooms. The children presently have no class rooms and they are sitting outside the class rooms in the school premises, affecting their educational activities. The counsel submits that thought plaintiff and his wife are OS.No. 2431/2024 staying in the suit schedule premises, their occupation Muniraju M vs Reeni on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40571489/ 6 is unauthorized without any authority either by the School or department. 11(b). The counsel further submits that utmost the plaintiff and his wife staying in the school premises as a licencee on permission, once license or permission are revoked, they have no right or authority to continue. The plaintiff's wife is not party to the suit. She has not filed any suit. The plaintiff is not connected with the suit. The plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands and he is not entitled for discretionary relief of permanent injunction and prayed for dismissal of suit. 12.
